requirement: Dependency execution does not silently broaden or shrink declared scope

files.note: Selected; preloads and calls the excluded vendor.gd. Path is relative to this oracle's own directory (pilot/fixtures/oracles/), not the usual pilot/fixtures/-relative convention, since this fixture lives under pilot/adapter-run/ -- it needs a real end-to-end GUT+gd-tools run, not a standalone driver, to observe the runtime effect of calling excluded code.
Excluded by gd-tools' default addons/ rule, but actually loaded and executed at runtime by app.gd.

measured_with_gd_tools_0_4_0.finding: Calling excluded vendor.gd from selected app.gd neither crashes instrumentation nor broadens the plan -- vendor.gd never appears in plan.json despite executing successfully at runtime, and app.gd's own line (the one calling into vendor.gd) is correctly measured as hit.

notes: A third real, verified positive finding (with F003 and F004): gd-tools' scope boundary holds even when excluded code is genuinely reachable and executed, not just present on disk unused. This is a stronger test than F004 alone, which only checked static file discovery -- F005 confirms the exclusion survives actual cross-boundary execution.
